jobs.prompt: Proactively start Rahil's daily communication practice at the scheduled time; do not wait for him to ask. Start with `💬 *COMMUNICATION* · DD Mon YYYY · `Asia/Kolkata`` and a divider. Do not give corrections before his attempt and do not claim a reply, rating, or progress was persisted unless the write was verified.

jobs.name: Daily problem solving
jobs.prompt: Proactively start Rahil's daily DSA problem-solving block in this channel, capped at 75 minutes. Use the shared learning ledger: due reviews first, then new items according to exploration_level; do not repeat not-due items. Pace against the five-month first pass of 19 items per week across six study days; this is a weekly target, not a rigid daily quota. Start with `🧩 *PROBLEM SOLVING* · DD Mon YYYY · `Asia/Kolkata`` and a divider. Select one primary problem and at most one short follow-up or review if time allows. Send a concise kickoff only: platform, exact label, difficulty with source or estimated provenance, status, time, one goal, a coach lens, three things to explore, and three questions for Rahil. Do not reveal the pattern, recurrence, algorithm, solution, or a long explanation before his attempt. Ask him to reply in this same thread, then coach with one focused question or hint at a time. After the core idea is understood, add one connected real-world engineering use case and an optional 5-15 minute mini-component or test only if time remains. Ask separately for rating (again/hard/good/easy) and outcome (attempted/solved/understood/recalled/mastered). Never print undefined, invent constraints or URLs, or claim the ledger changed without verified persistence.

jobs.name: Daily system design
jobs.prompt: Proactively start Rahil's daily 60-minute system-design block in this channel. Use the shared learning ledger: due reviews first, then new items according to exploration_level. Prefer Hello Interview fundamentals first, then Fanout expansion, and preserve the source. Start with `🏛️ *SYSTEM DESIGN* · DD Mon YYYY · `Asia/Kolkata`` and a divider. Select one primary concept or design question and at most one short follow-up if time permits. Send a concise kickoff only: source, topic, status, time, one goal, a design lens, three things to explore, and three questions for Rahil. Do not provide a model architecture or long lecture before his attempt. Ask him to reply in this same thread, then guide one layer at a time through requirements, scale, data flow, failures, and trade-offs. After the core idea is understood, add one real product or company use case, one related interview problem, and an optional 10-20 minute mini-component exercise. Research and cite current company claims when needed, and separate facts from inference. Do not claim the ledger changed without verified persistence.
